title: Supplier Crypto, KMS & Key Rotation Exhibit (Draft)
content:
Purpose and scope:
This exhibit (the "Crypto & KMS Exhibit") is intended to be appended to a Master Services Agreement or Data Processing Addendum to capture operational and contractual obligations specifically related to cryptographic key management, key rotation, and related operational controls for suppliers ("Supplier") providing services to Redwood Inference ("Customer").

Status: draft notes / working doc
- This is a negotiation-focused draft. It intentionally contains optional provisions (labeled [OPTIONAL]) to help Sales/Legal choose what to push for.
- Questions for legal: define acceptance criteria for FIPS/HSM attestations (third-party report types).

1) Definitions (short, contract-friendly)
- "Customer Key": cryptographic key material that is created or imported by Customer (including BYOK) and designated as Customer Key in writing or via the KMS interface.
- "Provider Key": cryptographic keys created and managed by Supplier to protect Supplier-managed secrets (not Customer Key).
- "KMS": Key Management Service used to generate, store, access, and rotate Customer Keys (could be Supplier-hosted or Customer-managed as agreed).
- "HSM": Hardware Security Module used for root-of-trust operations and key protection.
- "BYOK": Bring Your Own Key, a deployment option enabling Customer to import keys into Supplier KMS or configure supplier to use Customer-managed KMS.

2) High-level obligations (contract language intent)
- Supplier shall use commercially reasonable technical and organizational measures to protect Customer Keys, including storing keys in FIPS 140-2 Level 2 or Level 3 certified HSMs (where applicable), and restricting key material export except as permitted below.
- For Customer Keys, Supplier shall not access or use plaintext key material except as directed by Customer or to perform cryptographic operations on behalf of Customer where the operation is authorized by Customer and logged.

3) Key ownership, control and BYOK options
- Ownership: Customer retains exclusive legal ownership of Customer Keys. Supplier obtains only the limited rights necessary to perform the Services.
- BYOK options (choose one or more in the SOW):
  a) Customer-managed KMS (recommended when regulated data): Customer operates its own KMS; Supplier integrates and performs cryptographic operations via Customer-managed endpoints.
  b) Supplier-hosted KMS with customer-supplied key material (imported BYOK): Customer imports key material into Supplier HSM/KMS; imported keys are marked as Customer Keys and subject to all Customer Key protections.
  c) Supplier-hosted KMS with Supplier key generation and Customer key-wrapping: Supplier generates keys but wraps them with Customer Key material supplied via an import or external wrapping protocol.

4) Key lifecycle requirements
- Key generation: Keys used to protect Customer Data shall be generated in an HSM or via an approved cryptographic entropy source. For BYOK imports, Supplier shall verify integrity of the import process and annotate key provenance.
- Key usage policies: Keys must be scoped by purpose (e.g., data-encryption-key, signing-key), algorithm, and allowed services. Supplier must enforce purpose-limiting policies at the KMS/API level.
- Key rotation: Supplier shall support automated key rotation with configurable rotation periods. Unless Customer specifies otherwise, rotation for data-encryption keys shall occur no less frequently than every 12 months and for signing keys no less frequently than every 24 months. Rotation actions must preserve decryptability of previously encrypted data via key-wrapping or envelope encryption patterns, or a documented migration plan must be provided prior to rotation.
- Emergency rotation: Supplier must provide a documented process for emergency rotation (e.g., suspected compromise) including communication timelines and rollback/dual-key options.
- Key retirement & destruction: Supplier shall provide verifiable deletion of key material upon Customer request or at contract termination, except where retention is required by law. Supplier shall provide a signed certificate of destruction for HSM-resident keys or a verifiable audit record for KMS imports.

5) Access controls, dual control, and privileged operations
- Dual control for root operations: Any root key generation, import, export, or deletion in an HSM must require a dual-control (two-person) approval process and be logged.
- Separation of duties: Suppliers shall enforce role-based access controls (RBAC) so that no single operator has unilateral ability to (a) modify KMS policies that enable exfiltration and (b) perform key export.
- Privileged login: Privileged access shall require MFA, just-in-time access, and session recording for administrative sessions interacting with HSM/KMS.

6) Logging, monitoring and retention
- Cryptographic operation logs: Supplier shall log successful and failed key management operations (create, import, export attempts, rotate, destroy, grant, revoke) with user identity, timestamp, originating IP, and operation parameters.
- Key access telemetry retention: Logs for Customer Key operations shall be retained for at least 365 days unless Customer requests otherwise. Logs must be exportable to Customer or a Customer-designated log collector in structured format (e.g., JSON with field definitions).
- Alerts: Supplier must provide configurable alerting for sensitive events such as unauthorized export attempts, multiple failed access attempts, or emergency rotations.

7) Cryptographic standards and algorithms
- Minimum algorithms: Supplier shall support AES-256-GCM for symmetric data encryption, RSA-3072 or ECDSA P-384 for signing where public-key needed, and SHA-2 family for hashing, unless otherwise agreed.
- Algorithm deprecation: Supplier will notify Customer at least 180 days in advance of deprecating any algorithm used in Customer Keys and provide a migration plan.

8) Export, escrow, and lawful access
- Key export: Export of Customer Key material (plaintext) from Supplier-managed HSM/KMS is prohibited except (i) when Customer explicitly requests and documents the export, (ii) for lawful process with appropriate notification as allowed under the Agreement, or (iii) as required by statute (with Supplier's obligation to notify Customer where permitted).
- Key escrow [OPTIONAL]: If Customer requires escrow, Supplier shall store escrowed key material in a mutually agreed third-party escrow service and provide access controls and audit reports for escrow retrieval events.

9) Subprocessors and subcontractors
- Subprocessor usage: Supplier shall not allow subprocessors to access plaintext Customer Key material unless expressly authorized by Customer in the SOW. Supplier must flow down equivalent KMS controls and audit rights to any subprocessor handling key material.
- Onboarding checklist: Supplier must provide security profile of any subprocessor before onboarding, including HSM vendor, certification level, geographic location of key storage, and contact for emergency key operations.

10) Audit, attestation and compliance
- Attestations: Supplier shall provide annual third-party attestation reports relevant to cryptography controls (e.g., SOC 2 + CC6.6 mapping, FIPS/HSM module certification evidence). For customers in regulated sectors, Supplier shall provide additional artifact types as reasonably requested (e.g., HSM vendor test results).
- Audit rights: Customer shall have the right to audit Supplier's KMS environment with 30 days notice, subject to a mutually agreed scope that protects Supplier confidential information. Supplier shall reasonably cooperate and provide test accounts or redacted logs as needed.

11) Incident handling and breach notification
- Compromise definition: For the purposes of this exhibit, a "key compromise" is unauthorized access or suspected extraction of plaintext Customer Key material or successful cryptanalytic attack that materially weakens key confidentiality.
- Notification timeline: Supplier shall notify Customer within 24 hours of becoming aware of a key compromise.
- Remediation obligations: Supplier shall execute emergency rotation and a forensics plan at Supplier expense where compromise is confirmed, and shall provide remediation reports and evidence of destruction of compromised material.

12) Testing and acceptance
- Crypto integration testing: Supplier shall provide test vectors and a staging KMS environment to allow Customer to validate BYOK/import, wrap/unwrap, and rotation behaviors prior to production cutover.
- Acceptance criteria: Successful round-trip encryption + decryption, rotation without data loss, export controls enforced, and logs produced in agreed format.

13) Pricing / operational impacts
- Optional fee: BYOK import, dedicated HSM tenancy, or extended key retention may incur additional fees. These must be stated in the SOW.

14) Transition and termination assistance
- Export under termination: Following termination, Supplier shall provide orderly key export and assist with migration to Customer or successor provider under secure channel and mutually agreed timeline. Supplier shall not withhold Customer Key material as a condition of payment except as allowed by law.

15) Sample contract clause (language for insertion)
- "Supplier shall protect Customer Keys as set forth in the Crypto & KMS Exhibit. Supplier shall use HSMs certified to FIPS 140-2 Level 2 or higher for the storage and use of root key material. Supplier shall not export plaintext Customer Key material without the Customer's prior written consent. In the event of suspected key compromise, Supplier will notify Customer within 24 hours and follow the remediation and rotation procedures described in the Exhibit."

Open items / negotiation points (internal notes):
- Decide whether to require FIPS 140-2 Level 3 for all enterprise customers (pros: stronger assurance; cons: cost & availability).
- Escrow: whether to offer escrow as standard or priced add-on.
- Audit frequency & scope: propose annual attestation + targeted on-site audit rights for high-risk customers.

Appendix A: Implementation checklist for Sales/SE
- Select BYOK option in SOW (A/B/C).
- Confirm HSM vendor and cert level if customer requests.
- Add fees for dedicated HSM or extended log retention.
- Schedule integration testing in staging; attach test vectors (link to internal repo).
- Obtain signed destruction/retention certificate at contract end.

References / internal links: CONFLUENCE-SEC-CRYPTO-42 (design notes), JIRA SAND-2198 (KMS feature work), infra-kms-prototypes repo (implementation experiments).
